patients.summary: Healthy young woman, a junior marketing consultant, who joined the practice at 21. Her chart is a run of sexually transmitted infections handled mostly by outside gynecology and dermatology: vulvar condylomata (2019-2021), molluscum (2020), disseminated gonococcal infection with an admission (2023), and genital HSV-2 with a primary episode (2024) and one recurrence (2026).

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. No organisms identified.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21F here to set up primary care. Hasn't had a regular doctor since aging out of her pediatrician. No complaints today.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with hypothyroidism, father with hypertension, one sibling who is healthy.
SH: works as a junior marketing consultant. Never smoker. Alcohol occasionally, a drink or two socially on weekends. No drugs. Sexually active with men, uses condoms some of the time. No contraception and not interested in starting any right now. LMP about 2 weeks ago, regular cycles.

ROS negative across the board.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals reviewed. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid normal size, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rashes. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal, Pap and GC/CT swab collected.

A/P: healthy 21 year old, new to us.
- Pap today (first one).
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. TSH given mom's thyroid disease.
- One-time HIV and hep C screens; GC/CT.
- Tdap today, last one was at age 11 per her mother.
- Talked about HPV vaccine, she never got the series as a teen. She wants to read up on it first, will revisit.
- Condoms discussed.
- Flu shot when available next month.
- Will request old records from the pediatric office.

documents.title: Immunization Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS given. Screening questions all no. Tolerated well, no reaction in the 15 minutes after.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Isabelle, your blood work came back looking good: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and thyroid are all in the normal range. HIV, hepatitis C, gonorrhea and chlamydia tests were all negative. The Pap result usually takes another few days and I'll send that along when it's in.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap came back normal. Next one in three years, so fall 2021.

documents.title: RE: Pap result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: great, thank you!!

documents.title: Records Received: Pediatric Office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from her former pediatric office, 11 pages, scanned to chart. Immunization record and well-child visits through age 18.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pediatric records reviewed. Routine childhood series complete including MMR x2, varicella x2, hep B x3, MenACWY with booster, Tdap at 11. No HPV doses on file, which matches what she told me. Nothing else of note in the well-child history.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after work for flu shot. Quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. No egg or vaccine reactions in the past. VIS reviewed. Fine afterward.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly check. Feels well. Work busy but fine. No new problems since last fall.

Meds none. NKDA.
SH unchanged: never smoker, social drinking on weekends. Sexually active, more than one partner this year, condoms inconsistent. Still no contraception, declines again.

Exam: well. Vitals reviewed, weight steady. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Skin clear. Declined external genital exam today, no symptoms.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P: well visit.
- GC/CT urine. CBC, CMP.
- Flu shot given.
- Raised HPV vaccine again; still undecided.
- Pap not due until 2021.
- Condoms, and we can test any time if she has a new partner or symptoms.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything from Tuesday is normal, including the gonorrhea/chlamydia urine test. See you next year.

orders.reason: vulvar growths, likely condylomata, for biopsy and treatment

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in about bumps "down there" she first noticed sometime around late October. They don't hurt. Mostly she is embarrassed by how they look and was nervous to bring it up. No fever, no burning with urination, no discharge.

O: Vitals fine. External genital exam with MA chaperone: several cauliflower-like growths on the vulva. No inguinal nodes.

A/P: Most likely genital warts. Given the number and size I'd like gyn to look, biopsy one, and treat.
- Referral to gynecology placed, she prefers a female gyn if possible.
- GC/CT, HIV, RPR today since we're testing anyway.
- Explained warts come from HPV, common, treatable. Encouraged condoms. HPV vaccine still worth considering.

documents.title: Test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All negative: gonorrhea, chlamydia, HIV and syphilis. Gyn's office should be calling you to set up the appointment. Let me know if you haven't heard by next week.

documents.title: RE: Test results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They called! I go on the 24th. Thank you for being so nice about all this

medications.sig: Apply a thin layer to the warts at bedtime three times a week; wash off after 6-10 hours. Use for up to 16 weeks.

reports.text:
Specimen: vulva, shave biopsy of exophytic lesion.
Gross: one tan, papillary fragment of skin, 0.4 x 0.3 x 0.2 cm, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: squamous mucosa with papillary architecture, acanthosis and hyperkeratosis. No dysplasia identified.
reports.conclusion: Vulva, biopsy: squamous cell papillomatosis, consistent with condyloma acuminatum. Negative for dysplasia.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Gynecology consultation. Date of visit 12/24/2019.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Thayer, 22, at your request for genital lesions she has had for about two months. They are not painful, but she is bothered by how they look. She has had no fevers, urinary symptoms or vaginal discharge.

Medical history unremarkable. No surgeries. No medications. No known drug allergies. Family history of hypothyroidism in her mother and hypertension in her father; a sibling is well. She reports more than one sexual partner and does not use condoms every time.

On exam there are several cauliflower-like growths, 1 to 2 cm each, on the vulva. No lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the exam is normal.

We shave biopsied one lesion in the office. Pathology returned on 12/27 showing squamous cell papillomatosis without dysplasia, consistent with condyloma acuminatum. I called her with the result and sent imiquimod 5% cream to use at bedtime three nights a week, washed off in the morning, for up to 16 weeks. I explained that local redness and irritation are expected and that she can pause for a few days if it becomes too sore. She should come back if the lesions are not clearly better in two to three months.

Thank you for the referral.

Gynecology

documents.title: Prior Authorization: Imiquimod
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed a PA request for imiquimod 5% cream written by her gynecologist. Gyn's office already submitted on their end; insurer approved through 4/2020. Pharmacy notified. Nothing needed from us, filed for reference.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/03/2020
Referred by: primary care

Reason for consult: several small skin lesions over the past two weeks.

History: 23-year-old woman seen by gynecology in late December for vulvar condylomata. About two weeks ago she noticed one papule on the inner thigh and ignored it; a few more have come up in the same area since. They are not painful or itchy and have not drained. No prior skin problems like this. No fevers or other systemic symptoms. She had one day of diarrhea about three weeks ago that settled without treatment.

Problems: condylomata acuminata.
Medications: imiquimod 5% cream (vulva).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother hypothyroidism, father hypertension, sibling healthy.
Social: marketing consultant. Sexually active, new partner.

Vitals within normal limits.

Exam: inner thigh and adjacent skin with several small, firm, skin-colored, dome-shaped papules with central umbilication. Remainder of the examined skin unremarkable.

Assessment: molluscum contagiosum.

Plan: discussed that this is a self-limited viral infection that usually clears on its own over months. She prefers to let it run its course rather than have the lesions treated. Avoid shaving or picking the area; can spread by skin contact including with partners. Return if they spread widely or become inflamed.

Dermatology

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm consult from 4/3 reviewed. Thigh papules are molluscum. Plan is to watch, no treatment. Added to problem list.

documents.title: they're back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The growths are coming back near the opening :( Started itching a few weeks ago and they're getting bigger. I finished the cream in April. Should I go back to gyn or the skin doctor?

documents.title: RE: they're back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry, that's frustrating but not unusual with warts. Dermatology can do freezing in the office and has an opening Monday the 22nd. I sent the referral, they'll call you today. If you'd rather go back to gyn, that works too, just tell me.

procedures.procedure: Destruction of benign lesions, up to 14

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology clinic note. Visit date 06/22/2020.

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Thayer returns, previously seen by gynecology in December and by our clinic in April. For roughly three weeks she has had vulvar itching with mild discomfort and has noticed growths near the vaginal opening that are slowly getting larger. LMP 10 days ago, normal. She has had two male partners in the past year and does not always use condoms. No abnormal discharge, fevers or dysuria.

Problem list: condylomata acuminata; molluscum contagiosum.
Medications: none current (imiquimod course completed).
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: along the labia minora and posterior introitus there are multiple soft, exophytic, pink papules with a verrucous surface, 5 to 10 mm. Vagina and cervix look normal. No bleeding, no discharge.

Assessment: recurrent condylomata acuminata.

Procedure: after verbal consent, cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen, two freeze-thaw cycles to each visible lesion. Tolerated well. Expect blistering and soreness for several days; sitz baths and plain petrolatum for comfort.

We will see her back as needed. Condoms reduce but do not eliminate transmission; HPV vaccination remains reasonable at her age.

Dermatology

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm note from 6/22 reviewed: recurrent vulvar condylomata, cryotherapy done. Will check at her fall physical.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chief complaint: vulvar itching, mild discomfort.

HPI: Back again with itching and mild soreness for about three weeks and growths near the vaginal opening that have been getting bigger. Same thing as June, she says. Previously seen by gyn (Dec 2019, biopsy-proven condyloma, imiquimod), derm in April (molluscum) and derm in June (cryo for recurrence). LMP 10 days ago, normal. No abnormal discharge, no fever, no pain with urination.
SH: two male partners in the past year, condoms not every time.

Exam (MA chaperone): multiple soft, pink, exophytic lesions with a verrucous surface, roughly 5 to 10 mm, along the labia minora and posterior introitus. Speculum: vagina and cervix normal, no bleeding or discharge. Inner thighs clear now, no papules.

A/P:
1. Recurrent condylomata. Restart imiquimod 5% three nights a week, up to 16 weeks; recheck in about 4 months, sooner if not improving or too irritated. Could do cryo again if the cream doesn't work.
2. Molluscum, resolved.
3. High-risk sexual behavior. Spent time on this today: condoms with every partner, testing with each new partner, how HPV recurs. She was receptive. GC/CT today.
4. HPV vaccine: she's ready. Gardasil 9 dose 1 today; dose 2 in 1-2 months, dose 3 at 6 months. Explained it won't clear what she has but protects against other types.

documents.title: Immunization Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Gardasil 9 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, dose 1 of 3. VIS given. Sat 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gonorrhea and chlamydia negative. Happy new year, and we'll see you for Gardasil #2 in late February.
